title: Execution of a tableau layer
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $n$ be a natural number, let $z$ be a Boolean word, and let $T,t,\ell,ps$ be natural numbers. Assume $1\le T$ and $t\le T$. Starting at the layer label whose initial-step flag is true exactly when $t=0$, with the register values specified by the layer-start record for $(n,z,T,t,\ell)$ and input position $ps$, the counter program can execute in at most $B$ steps to the copy-loop label when $t=0$, and to the layer label otherwise. Here $B=k(2T+3)(L+20)+( |z|+n+2)(L+20)+(L+3)+9(T+1)D+6$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes, $L$ is the maximum template length, and $D$ is the stride determined by $M,n,z,T$. The final register values are those of the layer-start record for $(n,z,T,t+1,\ell)$, except that its $q$ register is set to $0$ when $t=0$ and otherwise to $(t+1)D-D$. The output is extended by the concatenation, over all indices $i$ from $tD$ through but excluding $(t+1)D$, of the Boolean encoding of the instruction for position $i$ in the tableau, and the execution property holds for every output prefix.
